Synopsis:
    Bond markets globally are under severe pressure as rising inflation — driven by a surge in Brent crude above $108/bbl (up 50%+ from July lows) and geopolitical disruption in the Strait of Hormuz and Bab al-Mandab Strait — forces yields sharply higher. US 10-year Treasury yields are approaching the critical 5% threshold. A key US CPI print is the immediate catalyst, with markets pricing a 70% chance of a Fed rate hike the following Wednesday. The "higher for longer" rate narrative is solidifying, with the Gulf conflict seen as a persistent inflationary tailwind.
